stories.headline: Flydubai captain recounts fighting off an alleged cockpit attack to prevent a crash

sources.body:
The Indian pilot of the Flydubai plane who was stabbed by his co-pilot and opened the cockpit door to let others in has said he was determined not to let others die.

Capt Smit Machchhar said he was on the floor and still being attacked when he realised the plane carrying more than 170 passengers was sinking and he had to do something.

"I was lying on the floor injured but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside," he said in a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

"Others came in and also played a role [in controlling the situation]. I was of course fighting for my own life but at the same time I knew I was not going to let others die," he added.

Flydubai's flight FZ1073, which was bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai early on Wednesday morning, plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey.

It first sent an emergency signal to air traffic controllers before switching to code squawk 7500, which indicates hijacking.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told the media that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane.

After fellow passengers overpowered the attacker, two reserve pilots, who were onboard, safely landed the plane at Tabuk Airport in north-western Saudi Arabia at 06:58 local time.

Machchhar, who has been hailed as a "true hero" by Netanyahu, was taken to hospital in Tabuk before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

Netanyahu told Fox News the attacker was an Omani national and said investigations suggested he had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination" .

He said that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question".

The United Arab Emirates has begun investigating "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose", according to the country's state news agency.

Indian social media has been awash with praise for Machchhar since his identity emerged.

He told Modi he had been flying planes for 17 years and "can tell what is happening to the plane even with my eyes closed".

The prime minister told him that "his courage, patience and quick decision-making saved the lives of so many people" and the whole country was proud of him.

The Indian embassy in the UAE on Thursday said Machchhar was "in good health and recovering well". Ambassador Deepak Mittal said he was "proud of Capt Smit for his bravery" and "very reassured" to meet him.

"I am not looking at this wound like a wound because that would make my recovery even more difficult," Machchhar said.

"I am looking at it as a journey which is slowly going on and will take time but I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again."
sources.headline: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot

sources.body: Smit Machchhar, the Indian captain who was attacked by his co-pilot onboard the Flydubai flight 1073 in an apparent attempt to crash the plane, on Friday told Prime Minister Narendra Modi that although he was severely injured in the altercation, “I could not let all those people die”. Although collapsed, he made a last-ditch effort and managed to push the door to the cockpit open.
sources.headline: Flydubai hero pilot tells Modi 'I could not let all those people die'

sources.body:
Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up then ‘passengers would lose their lives’

The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight has described how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.

Capt Smit Machchhar, who is recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, told the Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, in a video call broadcast live on television news channels that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save the passengers onboard.

“I had so many wounds. I had fallen down,” he said on Friday from the hospital, his head bandaged and tubes in his nose, before breaking down as he recalled the attack.

“I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realised that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives,” he told Modi.

Machchhar, who is from Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday’s attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker as the Boeing 737 descended sharply, witnesses and Israeli authorities said. He has been hailed as a hero for his actions, with world leaders saying he helped prevent a potential disaster.

The flight, carrying 182 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing.

The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said the attacker, an Omani national, was arrested in Saudi Arabia and was undergoing interrogation there. His motive for the attack remains unclear.

Machchhar said that during the difficult moments, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa, a devotional hymn dedicated to the Hindu deity Hanuman and traditionally recited as a prayer for strength and courage.

“Lord Hanuman gave me courage,” he told Modi.

Machchhar, who is married and has two children, has worked for flydubai for about four years, according to his LinkedIn profile. Before joining the airline, he spent 11 years with SpiceJet, an Indian low-cost carrier, where he served as a senior commander and line training captain. He logged more than 9,750 flying hours with SpiceJet.
sources.headline: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack

stories.headline: US military buildup raises fears of escalation in the Iran war as a tanker is hit in the Strait of Hormuz

sources.body:
By the end of November, three US aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be positioned near Iran.

The United States is deploying a third aircraft carrier strike group to waters in the Middle East close to Iran, a US official has told Al Jazeera, as the war enters its eighth month and both sides weigh escalation and diplomatic engagement.

Thousands more troops are also on their way to the region, just a month before November US midterm elections, which could see US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party hit hard by his handling of the war, which is deeply unpopular in the US.

We look at what the latest troop deployment means and whether it signals a coming escalation in the war on Iran:

A US official told Al Jazeera that the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group left its San Diego base on Sunday, bound for the region, followed a day later by the Makin Island Marine Expeditionary Unit (MEU), which is carrying more than 2,000 Marines.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the strike group and naval deployments could involve an additional 9,000 to 10,000 US troops in total, including sailors and Marines assigned to the carrier strike group and other ships.

By the end of November, the official said, three aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be positioned near Iran.

The official said the concentration of force would hand President Donald Trump a wider menu of options if he decides to act.

Al Jazeera’s Tanya Noury, reporting from Washington, said the new deployment, which includes F-35 fighter jets, will add to the roughly 50,000 US service members already stationed in the region.

The goal, Noury said, quoting sources inside the Pentagon and White House, is to keep military options “on the table” for Trump regardless of how diplomacy unfolds. The Pentagon is not currently planning to withdraw any assets even if an agreement with Iran is reached.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said forces are “ready to go” should Trump order new attacks.

The US has stationed troops and military assets at bases in the Middle East for decades.

According to the Council on Foreign Relations, the US operates from a broad network of military sites, both permanent and temporary, across at least 19 locations in the region.

Of these, eight are permanent bases, located in Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

The US’s first deployment of soldiers in the Middle East took place in July 1958, when combat troops were sent to Beirut during the Lebanon crisis. At its height, there were almost 15,000 Marines and soldiers in Lebanon.

As of mid-2025, there were 40,000 to 50,000 US soldiers stationed around the Middle East, comprising personnel stationed in both large, permanent bases and smaller forward sites across the region.

Trump has been beefing up the US military presence in the Middle East since the start of this year, initially sending warships, including the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, to the Arabian Sea.
sources.headline: New aircraft carrier, 10,000 US troops: Is the Iran war about to escalate?

stories.headline: US pressure on Europe to release diesel reserves follows fuel-price surge and possible export ban

sources.body: The United States on Thursday urged European allies to release strategic diesel reserves immediately to curb prices driven higher by the US war on Iran. EU states will discuss a coordinated response on Friday, as Washington increases pressure following US President Donald Trump's suggestion that he could ban US diesel exports.
sources.headline: US presses Europe to release diesel reserves 'immediately' as Trump threatens export ban

sources.body:
We're about to hear from several live guests, including RAC head of policy Simon Williams.

We'll also be hearing from people impacted by higher diesel prices - including a farmer and haulage company.

You can follow along at the top of the page by tapping watch live - we'll also bring you the key lines here.
sources.headline: Diesel hits £2 a litre in UK for first time, RAC says, as US pressures Europe to release reserves

sources.body:
In effort to avoid panic at pumps, Keir Mather insists supply of fuel to Britain is ‘inherently resilient’

UK diesel price hits record high of £2 a litre

The government has sought to avert panic at the pumps, insisting that the UK is not facing a diesel shortage after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel.

The transport minister Keir Mather said on Friday that the UK has a wide range of sources of the fuel and is in talks with other European countries over the potential release of emergency diesel stockpiles.

“I want to reassure people that they can still go to the pump and fill up with diesel because the supply we have to the UK is inherently resilient,” he said on ITV’s Good Morning Britain. “The flows of diesel into the UK come from a variety of sources, and that is resilient.

“The government’s obligation now is to work really closely with our partners [in Europe] and officials in the US administration to re-stress how important it is to have flows of diesel into the UK. People shouldn’t be concerned about shortages because of the inherent resilience that is built into that system.”

The UK relies on the US for about 30% of its diesel, with the vast majority coming from mainland Europe, and has reserve supplies for 42 days.

Earlier this week it emerged that the UK’s biggest refinery, Fawley in Hampshire, is set to shut for up to 10 weeks for planned maintenance. The UK had 18 refineries in the 1980s but now has only four.

On Thursday the UK opened talks with European allies over releasing emergency diesel supplies, after the Trump administration told Germany and France to release their stockpiles to help ease soaring prices or face a US supply ban.

The average price of a litre of diesel in the UK hit a record high on Friday, breaking the £2 mark for the first time, according to the motoring body the RAC.

“This is a pump price threshold that no one wanted to cross,” said Simon Williams, the head of policy at the RAC. “The average price of a litre of diesel has risen to a record 200.01p and is showing no signs of slowing, heaping more misery on to motorists.”

The government has extended the 5p cut in fuel duty until the end of the year. Earlier this week the RAC called on the government to extend the freeze into spring.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning

“We need to give people support where we can,” Mather said on GMB. “The government is not powerless. That is why we have a fuel duty freeze in place at the moment. The chancellor will set out the future of that at the budget, but is very aware of the impact that [high prices] are having on people.”

On Friday, Dan Jørgensen, the EU commissioner for energy, said Europe was discussing the question of whether to release emergency reserves of diesel with all members of the International Energy Agency, not only the US.

“This ‌is one of the ​opportunities that we have; we ⁠have used it before, ​and ​it is ​likely ​that ‌we ​would use ​it again,” he told Euronews.
sources.headline: UK is not facing diesel shortage despite fears of Trump export ban, minister says

stories.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as fighting in northern Ethiopia expands

sources.body:
Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises fears of a wider regional conflict.

On Thursday, Ethiopia announced that it was closing its embassy in the Eritrean capital, Asmara, and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security.

Eritrea responded by cutting diplomatic relations, saying Ethiopia's decision had left it with no choice but to take reciprocal action.

The diplomatic confrontation came hours after powerful explosions were heard overnight in Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa , including near Ethiopia's military headquarters.

It follows a sharp deterioration in relations between the neighbours, with Ethiopia accusing Eritrea of supporting a new rebel alliance – an allegation Asmara has repeatedly denied.

Eritrea described the decision to expel its ambassador as "astounding".

"Eritrea has no option but to reciprocate in kind and sever all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia," its foreign ministry said, warning of "negative corollaries" from the decision.

The diplomatic fallout comes as Ethiopian federal forces battle fighters from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and its allies across parts of the northern regions of Tigray, Afar and Amhara.

Ethiopia has also expelled an Egyptian diplomat, giving him 48 hours to leave the country, according to state media. The government has not publicly given a reason for the decision.

Egypt responded by ordering an Ethiopian embassy official to leave within the same period, according to the state-affiliated Al Qahera News.

Relations between Ethiopia and Egypt have been strained for years, largely over Ethiopia's Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), a huge hydroelectric project on the Blue Nile.

Egypt, which relies heavily on the Nile for its water supplies, has long expressed concern about the dam's potential impact on its share of the river's water.

The cutting of ties between Ethiopia and Eritrea mark a dramatic reversal from 2018, when Abiy restored relations with Asmara after two decades of hostility, prompting joyous scenes as the border reopened and families separated for years were reunited.

The rapprochement helped earn the Ethiopian prime minister the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019.

The latest hostilities are the most serious since a peace agreement ended the devastating Tigray war in 2022. An African Union mediator previously estimated that about 600,000 people had died during that two-year conflict.

Last month, the TPLF joined six other armed movements, including the Fano militia from Amhara, to form an alliance whose stated objective is to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government from power.

A pro-government militia commander fighting in Tigray told the BBC that Eritrean soldiers had been involved on the front lines.

The BBC has not independently verified the allegation.

The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and the internet has been cut, making it difficult to get reliable information from the region. It is not clear who was responsible for cutting communications.
sources.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates

sources.body:
Ethiopia says it will shut its embassy in Asmara, declares 10 Eritrean diplomats persona non grata.

Eritrea says it is breaking diplomatic ties with its neighbour Ethiopia in response to the expulsion of diplomats from Addis Ababa, as fighting between Ethiopia’s federal forces and a coalition of armed opposition groups intensifies .

“Eritrea has no option but to reciprocate in kind and sever all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia with all the negative corollaries that this entails,” its Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on X on Thursday.

This came shortly after Ethiopia announced it would close its embassy in Asmara “in response to Eritrea’s direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence against Ethiopia”.

Ethiopia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs also declared 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Ababa, including the charge d’affaires and others accredited to the African Union, “persona non grata for involvement in activities that pose a direct threat to Ethiopia’s national security”, requiring them to leave the country within 48 hours.

In its statement, Eritrea’s ministry said claims of its involvement in hostile activities were “astounding”.

“In reality, it is Ethiopia which has been pursuing an agenda of incessant hostility,” it said, adding that Addis Ababa had waged war against Eritrea to gain access to the Red Sea.

It also accused Ethiopia of hosting, training and arming Eritrean opposition groups to stoke internal conflict.

Addis Ababa has in turn accused Eritrea, ⁠Sudan and Egypt of supporting an opposition alliance led by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) that has fought against troops loyal to Ethiopia’s federal government since last week.

Ethiopia’s government also declared on Thursday an Egyptian diplomat persona non grata and ordered him to leave the country within 48 hours, according to the state-run Ethiopian Broadcasting Corporation.

Egypt responded in kind by declaring an Ethiopian embassy counsellor in Egypt persona non grata and giving him 48 hours to leave, the state-affiliated Al Qahera News reported, citing an Egyptian official.

Fierce clashes between Ethiopian federal forces and the armed opposition groups are continuing. On Wednesday and Thursday, explosions were heard in Addis Ababa, while fighters have also clashed with government forces in the northern Afar region .

In a statement on Thursday, United States Representatives Ilhan Omar, Jim McGovern, and John Garamendi expressed concern over the escalating fighting and called on all parties in Ethiopia to “immediately recommit to peace negotiations”.

“This increased conflict threatens the entire country and the region as a whole, which is already reeling from the previous war in Northern Ethiopia and the devastating conflict in Sudan. Ordinary civilians are bearing the brunt of this violence,” the statement reads.

Days after the latest clashes broke out last week, the chief administrator of the Afar region, Haji Awol ⁠Arba, told Al Jazeera that Eritrean soldiers had crossed into Afar to join the alliance’s offensive.
sources.headline: Eritrea severs diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in tit-for-tat move

sources.body:
Old rivalries, territorial disputes and new alliances are reshaping the conflict in Ethiopia’s north.

Fighting is intensifying across northern Ethiopia, almost four years after a peace deal ended a devastating two-year war in the country’s Tigray region.

The conflict has also spread into the neighbouring Amhara and Afar regions. Government-aligned forces say they captured the strategic town of Alamata, Tigray, on September 28, while Tigrayan forces have pushed into Afar.

Telecommunications have been cut across much of Tigray and commercial flights have been suspended, separating families and hampering humanitarian operations.

Ethiopia’s army chief has accused Eritrea, Sudan’s army and Egypt of backing the armed groups, raising fears of a wider regional war. All countries have denied the allegations, with Egypt adding that it strictly respects the sovereignty of neighbouring states.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera maps where the fighting is, who is involved and how Ethiopia got here.

Fighting is concentrated in three regions in northern Ethiopia: Tigray, Amhara and Afar. There are several active fronts rather than a single battlefield.

In southern Tigray, government forces and their allies have taken Alamata, a strategic town about 120km (75 miles) south of the regional capital, Mekelle.

The town is a supply hub for troops, fuel and food near Tigray’s border with Amhara.

On September 22, between 15 and 17 drone strikes hit Alamata, including several schools and a hospital, according to the conflict monitor ACLED.

To the west, a separate front has opened near the Tekeze River in western Tigray, an area disputed between Tigray and Amhara.

Fighting has also spread into northern Amhara, around Kobo and Gidan in North Wello zone and Sekota in Wag Hemra zone, which government forces retook on September 27.

Further east, Tigrayan forces and the Afar armed group Ugugumo have advanced into Afar, where fighting has been reported along the Tigray-Afar border and around Erebti and Abala.

The advance matters because it could threaten the Semera-Djibouti corridor, Ethiopia’s main route for imports, including fuel.

Seven Ethiopian armed and political groups announced an alliance on September 20 aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government and establishing an inclusive transitional government.

The group is called the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, or the Alliance for Survival. Its members include:

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) : The alliance’s main military force, whose fighters launched the latest offensive. It dominated Ethiopian politics for nearly three decades before Abiy took office in 2018. War broke out between the TPLF and federal forces in November 2020.

The Amhara Fano National Movement: A coalition of Fano factions that turned against Abiy’s government in 2023, after fighting alongside federal forces during the Tigray war.

The Oromo Liberation Army (OLA): It has fought federal forces in Oromia since 2018, seeking greater self-determination for the Oromo.
sources.headline: How the fighting in Ethiopia spread beyond Tigray, in maps and charts

stories.headline: Russia again strikes Kyiv’s Southern Bridge as attacks on the Ukrainian capital continue

sources.body: Russian drones on Friday hit Kyiv’s Southern Bridge for a fourth time in 24 hours, forcing authorities to close traffic on it. “They keep hitting it in the same place,” FRANCE 24’s Ukraine correspondent said, noting that it is one of Kyiv’s seven bridges and is extremely important to the life of the city. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments on the war in Ukraine.
sources.headline: Live: Russia hits Kyiv’s Southern Bridge again as Moscow continues to pound capital

sources.body:
Moscow has suffered further losses of occupied territory, but is using new drones to beat Ukraine’s defences ahead of winter.

Russia suffered its highest losses of 2026 in September, when 46,230 of its soldiers were killed or wounded, according to the Ukrainian military .

The new record comes after Russian casualties of about 40,000 a month since June, and is close to the goal Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy set in January of 50,000 Russian casualties a month. Russia reportedly lost 2,090 troops on September 28 – its highest 24-hour casualty rate of the war.

Al Jazeera cannot verify casualty claims from either side. Ukraine says it has video of each casualty, as more than 90 percent of them are caused by first-person view (FPV) drones.

But despite setbacks, Russia has been trying to seize the remaining areas of Ukraine’s eastern regions of Luhansk and Donetsk that it doesn’t control — which is where casualties have been heaviest.

Ukraine’s Third Army Corps has inflicted particularly heavy losses in the area around Lyman, where the third phase of a counteroffensive called Operation Vivaldi has reclaimed 176sq km (68sq miles) of territory in recent weeks.

Corps commander Brigadier General Andriy Biletsky said it succeeded by feigning an attack from the west, and “forced it [the Russian army] to senselessly burn through its reserves in counterattacks precisely in that direction”. Then it attacked from the north.

Among its tactics was the use of remotely operated Russian armoured personnel carriers filled with explosives that smashed into Russian defences.

A Ukrainian commander on the Lyman front described how Vivaldi’s first phase eliminated a vanguard of Russian soldiers. Ukrainian drone operators have also been busy disrupting Russian ammunition and fuel supplies, starving the front.

Russia denied the Ukrainian counteroffensive’s gains, posting videos as purported evidence .

Russia has frequently claimed to hold positions and gain territory. But assessments by the Institute for the Study of War and DeepState, organisations that track territorial gains using open source, geolocated footage, rarely reflect Russian claims on their maps.

The ISW has estimated Russia’s net gains this year at 148sq km (57sq miles), nowhere near the 5,300sq km that Russia claims.

Still, Russia pounded Ukraine’s cities during the past week, striking energy infrastructure but also residential buildings, kindergartens, schools, office buildings and other nonmilitary targets.

Several people were killed on September 28, when a drone destroyed part of the National Academy of Sciences in Kyiv.

Kyiv experienced power outages on September 30, when Russian drones struck a thermal power plant in the Kyiv region. At least five people were killed across the country.

“Since the summer, there has not been a single day when the enemy has not attacked energy infrastructure. However, such a massive and combined attack has not occurred since the end of the last heating season,” wrote Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi on social media.
sources.headline: Russia tries to freeze Ukraine as it suffers record casualties and retreats

stories.headline: Europe records widespread heat stress after a summer of heatwaves and excess deaths

sources.body: A record 52% of Europe faced intense heat stress this summer, the EU’s climate monitor said Friday, as climate change fuelled widespread heatwaves and tens of thousands of excess deaths. Europe recorded its third warmest summer, while western Europe experienced its hottest, with several countries setting national temperature records overall.
sources.headline: More than half of Europe faced intense summer heat stress, EU monitor says

sources.body:
EU Copernicus report shows surface air temperatures from June to August were 2.5C above decadal average

T he scorching heat that persistently baked western Europe this summer was the worst on record, a report has found, with more than half the continent seared by “very strong” heat stress that felt hotter than 38C.

Surface air temperatures in western Europe from June to August were 2.5C above the recent decadal average, according to an update from the EU’s Copernicus climate monitoring service on Friday, while milder but still deadly heat across the rest of the continent made the summer Europe’s third hottest on record.

The finding comes as a swelling El Niño of unprecedented strength raises global temperatures and supercharges violent weather from South America to Australia. The natural sea warming pattern, which has broken the temperature record months before its expected peak at the end of the year, is expected to cause almost half a million extra heat-related deaths by February.

In Europe, where El Niño’s effects are felt mostly indirectly – for instance, through higher food prices and inflation – the intense heat experienced this summer is the result of fossil fuel pollution clogging the atmosphere.

The report found at least 60% of western Europe suffered through temperatures above 30C on 17 days this summer. In 2003, a year also marked by ferocious heat, this was observed on 11 days, and in 2025 on just seven. The high heat led to a record-breaking 13 days of “very strong” heat stress across western Europe.

Europe saw an abnormally early start to summer-like weather when a powerful heatwave boggled climate scientists in late May, and high heat continued even through September, the report found. Recurring heatwaves, made hotter and more common by climate breakdown, killed tens of thousands of people across the continent while ruining harvests and shutting power plants.

“The consequences extended far beyond temperature records – affecting water availability, energy systems, transport, ecosystems and human health,” said Samantha Burgess, a climate scientist at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. “As the climate continues to warm, events like these underscore the importance of building resilience to increasingly interconnected climate risks.”

Compounding extremes of heat, drought and fire proved particularly damaging. European sea surface temperatures this summer also broke records, the report found, while the continent’s rivers experienced their lowest summer flows in more than 30 years. Hot weather and widespread drought helped wildfires run rampant.

The severity of fire weather conditions in 2026 was the worst that scientists have ever recorded, data published by the European Forest Fire Information System on Wednesday showed. By the end of September, the 680,000 hectares that were burned made it the third-worst on record, behind the million hectares burned by this time of year in 2025 and the 768,000 hectares burned in 2022.

Smoke, one of the greatest environmental threats to human health, spewed 30% more fine particulate matter into the air than the average over the last two decades.
sources.headline: May heatwaves, deaths, ruined harvests: study of Europe’s summer paints grim picture for the future

stories.headline: Christa Pike remains in critical condition after surviving a failed lethal-injection execution in Tennessee

sources.body: Pike is the first person to survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs, the Death Penalty Information Center said. She remains in a critical condition.
sources.headline: What to know about Christa Pike, her failed execution and what happens next

sources.body:
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike is in "critical condition, receiving life-saving care" at hospital, after surviving two lethal injection attempts, leading the state's governor to halt all executions for the year.

"We don't have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment," her lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters on Thursday. "But we do know that she is alive right now."

Her lawyers are now asking for her sentence to be commuted. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.

She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive, her lawyers said. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer.

Her attempted execution on Wednesday was the subject of a last-minute legal battle. This culminated in the US Supreme Court allowing the lethal injections to go ahead.

Slemmer's mother May Martinez, who was among those who wanted the execution to take place and who travelled to Tennessee to witness it, told NBC News after the botched attempt that "it was a mess".

On Thursday afternoon, Pike's lawyers offered more details about what happened during the attempted execution, describing a harrowing scene shrouded in secrecy.

"Last night, the execution team attempted to establish an IV line for an hour," Spivey said. "I counted at least seven needles used in her left arm alone, one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her arm after an unsuccessful attempt."

Spivey said that observers were kept in a dark room behind a closed curtain, after the second lethal dose had been administered and "it was clear that Miss Pike was still breathing" minutes later.

"No-one knew what was going on behind that curtain," Spivey said. "I had no idea when and if medical professionals began to assist."

Spivey said the state's governor must commute Christa's sentence now, a request that was denied previously.

Stephen Ferrell, another of Pike's lawyers, said they were also looking at other legal options.

"We want to think this through and we want to make sure that Christa recovers and has some input in what she wants," he said.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review and said on Thursday the investigation into Pike's botched execution "will be thorough", adding that "it's going to take time".

"There are a lot of questions," Lee said. "The people of our state deserve to have those questions answered, and that's what this investigation is for."

Lee has not made clear who will conduct the independent review of the state's execution procedures.

His order to pause all executions will overlap with the planned 3 December execution of convicted murderer Gary Sutton.

The Tennessee Department of Correction, which handled the execution, issued a statement defending its handling of the case.

It said in a statement that it "followed every step of the State's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the attorney general's office".
sources.headline: Christa Pike in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections, lawyer says

sources.body: Christa Pike continued breathing for nearly an hour after she was administered lethal drugs in Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.
sources.headline: What is a botched execution, and what happened in previous cases?

stories.headline: New York appoints Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in the Cornell fraternity rape case

sources.body: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Thursday said that she had lost faith in the county district attorney’s ability to fairly oversee the case and had appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor.
sources.headline: Unsealed documents detail Cornell investigation into alleged rape at fraternity house

sources.body:
New York state prosecutors have reopened an investigation into the alleged rape of a woman at Cornell University in 2024.

The woman filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university on 16 September alleging she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house at the university.

She also alleged that Cornell failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved.

The men have been dubbed the "Cornell Seven" and the woman was identified anonymously as Jane Doe in court filings.

Cornell has said it supported presenting the case to a grand jury, while rejecting claims that it failed to punish those involved. It has also agreed to have the case examined by an independent investigator.

In a 101-page civil lawsuit, the woman alleged that on the night of 19 October 2024, seven men from Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity chapter assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine.

She was a 20-year-old Cornell undergraduate at the time.

Jane Doe said in her lawsuit that she was intoxicated during the alleged incident and incapable of providing consent.

She said she left her sorority sisters after drinking that night and "stumbled alone" to the Chi Phi fraternity house in the city of Ithaca to see a male friend.

The lawsuit alleges sexual assault and battery, negligence, breach of contract and violations of New York's Human Rights Law.

It was filed against the university, fraternity sorority and men involved in the alleged attack.

The lawsuit contains an image purported to be from a fraternity group chat in which a participant alerted other members, in vulgar terms, to the potential for a sexual encounter with Doe.

Her lawyer has said she was "traumatised, numb and unable to function or accept the horror of what had happened" in the days after the assault, which she reported to Cornell University Police on 8 November 2024.

The outrage in recent weeks grew when Doe alleged in her lawsuit that the men were "afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays".

Doe's lawyer has said two of those involved were expelled. He has told CBS that the woman dropped out of university after the alleged assault.

Cornell newspaper's editorial board published the names of the defendants in the lawsuit on 21 September in a piece titled "Cornell Won't, We Will", fuelling outcry on social media.

The Cornell University Police Department provided an image of the Snapchat group, titled Chi Phi Actives, to prosecutors as evidence in November 2024, the university said.

The members are named in the chat and discuss a "free" sexual encounter with Jane Doe, using coarse language, just before 02:00 local time on 20 October 2024.

CBS News New York has also published excerpts of additional text messages reportedly exchanged between one of the defendants and a woman who appears to be the person who made the allegations.

The messages were reportedly sent two days after the alleged assault.

In one message, one of the men appeared to apologise for "how things went down".

stories.headline: Junts maintains opposition to Spain’s housing decrees, deepening pressure on Sánchez and raising early-election speculation

sources.body: <p>A pocos días de que se despeje el camino para el regreso a España de Carles Puigdemont, su partido ha puesto al Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez contra las cuerdas. La formación independentista ha expresado su rechazo a los dos decretos sobre vivienda elaborados por el Ejecutivo como respuesta a las movilizaciones sociales desatadas tras el desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal. Los independentistas, en una declaración divulgada anoche por su ejecutiva, exigen la retirada de los decretos y la elaboración de una nueva propuesta. Un pulso en toda regla al que el Gobierno tardó muy poco en responder y también con toda firmeza: los decretos no se retiran y se mantiene la previsión de que los vote este viernes el pleno del Congreso.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-02/junts-rechaza-los-decretos-de-vivienda-y-pone-al-gobierno-contra-las-cuerdas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Junts rechaza los decretos de vivienda y pone al Gobierno contra las cuerdas

sources.body:
Desde primera hora de la mañana ha pesado en el Congreso un ambiente de incertidumbre. El rechazo de Junts per Catalunya a los dos decretos de vivienda hacían imposible su convalidación; sin embargo, el Gobierno ha optado por mantener ambos textos y no tocar ni una coma. "Este Gobierno no va a dar un paso atrás en su lucha por el derecho a la vivienda", publicaba casi de madrugada el líder del Ejecutivo, Pedro Sánchez , en sus redes sociales.

"Ha llegado la hora de la verdad. PP, Vox y Junts deben elegir : o están con la mayoría social o con los especuladores. Mañana, su voto les retratará ante generaciones enteras", insistía Sánchez en su mensaje.

Varios ministros han apuntado en la misma dirección, que es la de presionar a estos partidos para que repiensen su voto. Una de las voces que ha apostado por la abstención de Junts es la titular de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez . "Quedan unas horas para la votación. Espero que cambien de opinión, se vayan a la abstención y permitan la tramitación del decreto como proyecto de ley urgente", ha dicho desde el patio de la Cámara Baja.

Sánchez ha llegado al Congreso minutos antes del inicio del Pleno. Ya una vez dentro del hemiciclo, la bancada socialista ha aplaudido largamente al jefe del Ejecutivo , quien también ha respondido con aplausos a los suyos.

Ya en la tribuna, Rodríguez ha hablado directamente a los siete diputados de Junts, capitaneados por Míriam Nogueras , que ha evitado en varias ocasiones mirar a la titular de Vivienda mientras le interpelaba. "Con ustedes hemos trabajado este texto y creo que es el día de hablarles con honestidad a la ciudadanía. Les vuelvo a pedir que puedan apoyar con su voto favorable o abstención el decreto ley . Es la hora de la verdad y de cumplir con españoles y catalanes", ha remarcado.

Isabel Rodríguez, para acercar posturas con los de Carles Puigdemont, ha emplazado a los diputados a facilitar la convalidación de los decretos y que se puedan tramitar a lo largo de las próximas semanas como proyecto de ley para así añadir "sus puntualizaciones o correcciones".

La titular de Vivienda también ha cargado duramente contra el PP, que ya ha dicho que votará en contra de los textos. "Si se ponen del lado de los buitres están inhabilitados para gobernar este país" , ha achacado la ministra a los diputados del PP. "Dónde están ustedes, por qué aún no han asumido que hablamos de un derecho y que hay que combatir la especulación. Señorías del Partido Popular, podrían ser útiles", ha dicho.

La portavoz de Junts, Míriam Nogueras, ha ratificado también desde la tribuna su 'no' a los dos decretos y ha instado al Gobierno a que los retire y negociar uno nuevo "a puerta cerrada". " Retiren los reales decretos y sigamos trabajando en un texto que dé soluciones de verdad al problema, pensando en la gente, a puerta cerrada", ha pedido en su intervención.

Además, Nogueras ha acusado este viernes al Gobierno y a su presidente, Pedro Sánchez, de "engañar a la gente", de "alimentar una mentira" y de darle una "falsa esperanza" con un decreto de vivienda que, a su juicio, ni frena los desahucios ni impide que la especulación.
sources.headline: El Gobierno mantiene los decretos a pesar del rechazo de Junts y se abre la posibilidad de un adelanto electoral

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez 

“Ha llegado la hora de la verdad”, ha advertido Pedro Sánchez en la noche del jueves, después de que Junts haya confirmado que este viernes votará en el Congreso contra los dos decretos ley de vivienda  aprobados por el Consejo de Ministros, lo que aboca a su derogación. En el Gobierno ven que la enorme indignación provocada por el desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal la semana pasada en Madrid, y las protestas sociales y acampadas en la Puerta del Sol y otras muchas plazas por toda España, han generado una movilización en la izquierda como hacía años que no conseguían. Y consideran, por tanto, que se abre una oportunidad que no hay que dejar pasar. “Es el momento de aprovechar para convocar elecciones”, asegura un ministro del PSOE a  La Vanguardia .

Ministros socialistas ya están apremiando al propio Pedro Sánchez, por tanto, a aprovechar el tirón de esta movilización social para presentar batalla a la derecha en las urnas. La primera fecha disponible para esta precipitación electoral, en caso de que la adopte el presidente del Gobierno, sería el próximo domingo 29 de noviembre, según barajan en el PSOE.

La determinación de Sánchez, hasta ahora, era convocar las elecciones en el 2027, con dos escenarios abiertos: en febrero o marzo, antes de las elecciones municipales y autonómicas de mayo, como demandaban precisamente muchos candidatos del PSOE a estos comicios; o ya en julio, para agotar la legislatura hasta el último suspiro como siempre fue su pretensión. El calendario previsto estaba vinculado, sobre todo, a los presupuestos generales del Estado para el 2027, que aún no ha aprobado el Consejo de Ministros pero ya está negociando el ministro de Hacienda, Arcadi España. El debate de totalidad del proyecto de cuentas públicas, antes de fin de año, estaba previsto que pudiera desencadenar los acontecimientos. Si el PP, Vox y Junts lo tumbaban, muchos en el PSOE que era el momento de convocar elecciones generales, y el proyecto de presupuestos se transformaría en el programa electoral de Sánchez.

La gestión de la crisis migratoria de Ceuta el pasado mes julio, pero aún sin resolver, alteró muchas de las predicciones, ya que ayudó a movilizar aún más a las derechas, y singularmente a Vox, mientras que desgastó aún más al Gobierno y al PSOE y empañó aún más sus perspectivas electorales. La prudencia y la cautela parecían invitar a aplazar el calendario de las elecciones generales, al menos hasta que Ceuta deje de surtir de gasolina electoral a la ultraderecha. Además, el espacio político a la izquierda del PSOE seguía sin recomponerse, y con muy malos augurios demoscópicos.

El dramático desahucio de Maricarmen la semana pasada en Madrid, y las protestas sociales que dispararon como un recordatorio de las movilizaciones del 15-M del 2011, fueron interpretadas en la Moncloa como una “oportunidad histórica” para tratar de resucitar la mayoría parlamentaria de la investidura en torno a un paquete “potente” de medidas sobre la vivienda que dieran respuesta a la indignación ciudadana. Esta renovada alianza de los grupos de la investidura, además, podía alentar renovadas esperanzas sobre los presupuestos generales del Estado y la continuidad del curso de la legislatura. Pero la decisión de Junts de tumbar los decretos ley del Gobierno ha cambiado el panorama de forma radical. Y, ahora, ministros y dirigentes del PSOE coinciden: es el mejor momento para las elecciones generales.
sources.headline: El Gobierno ve una oportunidad: “Es el momento de aprovechar para convocar elecciones”

stories.headline: Torrential rain triggers flooding alerts, transport disruption and school closures in eastern Spain

sources.body:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in Nepal

Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.

Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.

Meanwhile, heavy rainfall in Nepal last week resulted in 542 disaster incidents and left 27 people dead between 24 and 27 September, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Of the recorded incidents, 304 were related to landslides while 87 were linked to flooding.

During this extremely wet period, 186 meteorological sites recorded more than 100mm of rainfall, with Dedhgaun, in Lumbini province, recording 544.2mm. Nearly a million people received SMS flood warnings, and 2,000 people living in high-risk areas were relocated.

This heavy rainfall also affected the Gandak River in Bihar, north-east India, which reached a record water level of 91.25 metres on Tuesday, 0.35m metres above the previous record, set only in 2024, according to the water resources department. So far, 169 seepage points along the embankments have been repaired, with teams deployed across several sites along the river as the embankments continue to face heavy water pressure.

Strong winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding have hit the north-east US as a very deep area of low pressure developed into a nor’easter on Saturday. Such storms are named due to the north-easterly winds typically affecting coastal areas. This was the first nor’easter of the autumn and winter season, bringing gusts of up to 74mph (119km/h) and waves rising to 3 metres.

The storm left approximately 200,000 people without power, inundated the streets of New York City and killed one person when a tree fell in Brooklyn. However, the storm also uncovered a piece of history as the wreckage from the Warren Sawyer, a three-masted ship destroyed in 1884, washed ashore on Nantucket, off Cape Cod in Massachusetts.
sources.headline: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding

stories.headline: Spain’s September employment rises by 92,000, aided by migrant regularization

sources.body:
Un trabajador del sector de la construcción. / Archivo

La regularización extraordinaria de migrantes ha supuesto un arreón para el mercado laboral. No es que el mismo andara débil, especialmente teniendo en cuenta el contexto internacional y la mayor tibieza de economías vecinas, pero la inyección de centenares de miles de personas a la economía formal ha provocado un acelerón notable en las contrataciones . También, aunque con menor intensidad, en las listas del paro.

El empleo registró este pasado septiembre el mejor inicio de curso de los últimos 26 años. La Seguridad Social sumó 92.327 afiliados, hasta alcanzar un total de 22,43 millones de trabajadores en activo . Es el mejor registro en un mes de septiembre desde el año 2000. El paro , por su parte, subió en 23.587 personas, hasta un total de 2,3 millones de desempleados apuntados a las listas del Sepe.

La educación ha sido el sector que más ha tirado de las contrataciones, con 63.499 nuevas altas, algo habitual y previsible teniendo en cuenta el reinicio de las clases y las consecuentes llamadas para reincorporar a maestros en la privada y concertada, así como monitores, personal de comedor y academias, entre otros.

No obstante, el 'efecto regularización' se puede observar en aquellos sectores cuyos empresarios han manifestado mayor complacencia con la concesión de permisos de trabajo a las personas nacidas fuera pero que llevaban ya años viviendo y muchos de ellos trabajando 'en B'.

Por ejemplo, en la construcción se han incorporado tres veces más ocupados este septiembre respecto a agosto que el año pasado, en la hostelería el habitual recorte de empleo tras la campaña de verano ha sido menor y en las actividades administrativas o la agricultura ha habido un mayor número de contrataciones este año.

Según el balance realizado por la Seguridad Social, a día 30 de septiembre, se han dado de alta un total de 421.306 personas al empleo a través del proceso de regularización. Por nacionalidad, los afiliados que más peso tienen sobre el total proceden de Colombia y Venezuela , siendo el 71,1% de los nuevos afiliados de Latinoamérica.

La regularización extraordinaria de migrantes está ensanchando el mercado laboral. Este septiembre, si la Seguridad Social sumó unos 92.000 nuevos ocupados, 84.000 eran nacidos fuera. Hay más trasiego de gente, más profesionales cotizando -la Seguridad Social ha vuelto a la ratio 2,5 trabajadores por pensionista , algo que no se veía desde 2011-, pero también más gente apuntada a las listas del paro para tratar de encontrar un empleo.

El Sepe ha informado que el número de inscritos en sus oficinas de empleo ha aumentado en 23.587 personas respecto a agosto, hasta alcanzar un total de 2,37 millones de desempleados . No todos, ni mucho menos, son nuevos parados derivados de la regularización. De hecho, una persona que acabe de recibir papeles y pueda trabajar tiene pocos incentivos para inscribirse en el Sepe ya que no tiene derecho a una prestación contributiva al no haber cotizado previamente.
sources.headline: El empleo acelera, suma 92.000 ocupados y vive el mejor septiembre desde el año 2000

sources.body:
Los afiliados extranjeros ya suman un 16% del total 

La regularización de extranjeros mantiene su impacto en el mercado laboral, con la creación de 92.327 afiliados el mes pasado, lo que le convierte en el mejor septiembre desde que hay registros. Supone el triple de crecimiento que el registrado en el mismo mes del 2025, que ya fue muy positivo, e incluso queda por encima de los resultados del 2020, cuando se producía el rebote del desempleo a la salida de la pandemia. Las cifras detalladas muestran claramente cómo son los afiliados extranjeros los que marcan la diferencia. Suponen nueve de cada diez nuevos empleos. En cifras absolutas, 84.220 extranjeros del total de 92.327 que sumó el mes.

Otra característica destacada es que los nuevos afiliados son en su inmensa mayoría mujeres; suman el 98%. En concreto, son 90.859 mujeres por solo 1.468 hombres.

Ya en meses anteriores, la regularización marcó su influencia en el mercado laboral, cuando estos trabajadores, al legalizar su situación, se han dado de alta en la Seguridad Social. En agosto, por ejemplo, redujeron de forma significativa la caída del empleo. Ahora ya son 3,6 millones, más del 16% del total de cotizantes. Y el porcentaje va subiendo.

Si se realiza una fotografía del mercado laboral del día 30 de septiembre, los afiliados extranjeros regularizados en alta por el proceso de regularización sumaban 421.000, lo que supone 83.000 más que el último día de agosto. Dos países concentran casi la mitad de estos extranjeros regularizados, Colombia, con 118.000, y Venezuela, con 72.000.

El mercado laboral ha seguido en septiembre la tendencia habitual de este mes del año, aunque con la citada diferencia de este crecimiento extraordinario propulsado por los extranjeros recién regularizados. De esta manera, aparece cómo los profesores vuelven a clase después del verano, con 60.300 nuevos empleos. Se les había despedido durante las vacaciones y ahora se les ha contratado de nuevo. Este incremento compensa sobradamente la pérdida de 39.000 empleos en el comercio y de 19.500 en la hostelería. En la hostelería, por cierto, la reducción de afiliados es claramente inferior a la de septiembre del año pasado. En total, la suma de cotizantes es de 22,43 millones, acercándose al récord que se marcó en julio.

Si la regularización de extranjeros tiene un impacto en la afiliación, también lo tiene en el desempleo, aumentando el número de parados inscritos. Son personas que, una vez obtenidos los papeles, se apuntan al paro. De esta manera, la cifra global de parados se incrementó en 23.587 personas más, cuando en septiembre del año pasado el desempleo disminuyó y en ejercicios anteriores hubo aumentos, pero claramente inferiores.

Desde el Ministerio de Trabajo señalan que este incremento del paro es una elevación puntual, que viene por una inscripción de estos extranjeros que han obtenido la regularización antes de acceder al puesto de trabajo. “El paso por oficinas de empleo es un paso simplemente burocrático, previo a la contratación”, afirma el secretario de Estado de Trabajo, Joaquín Pérez Rey, añadiendo que es la empresa la que les sugiere que se apunten al paro y que después los contratarán. Argumenta también que en el 80% de los casos permanecen menos de dos meses inscritos en el desempleo.
sources.headline: La regularización acelera la creación de empleo, con 92.000 afiliados más en septiembre

sources.body:
La acampada por la vivienda de plaza Catalunya, en Barcelona, ha crecido de forma visible después de que se sumara este jueves por la noche el Sindicat de Llogateres / Manu Mitru

La acampada por la vivienda de plaza Catalunya , en Barcelona , ha crecido de forma visible después de que se sumara este jueves por la noche el Sindicat de Llogateres . Si el miércoles había unas 50 tiendas de campaña, a las diez de la noche de este jueves se contabilizaban alrededor de 200 .

El campamento ha recibido nuevos participantes después de la cacerolada convocada por la plataforma en la plaza Sant Jaume , que reunió a 800 personas según el Ayuntamiento y a 2.000 según los organizadores. Una vez instaladas las nuevas tiendas, se celebró una asamblea entre las personas participantes, en la que se hicieron llamamientos a convocar una huelga general como medida de presión para buscar una solución a la crisis de la vivienda.

El campamento va incorporando progresivamente servicios para atender a las personas que participan en la protesta. Se han instalado varias mesas, una especie de barra de bebidas, una caja de libros para quien quiera cogerlos y un "armario abierto" con ropa para quien la necesite. También hay un punto lila y un punto de información.

Acampada por la vivienda en la plaza Catalunya. / Lorena Sopêna / Europa Press

Entre las personas que han llegado este jueves por la noche al campamento hay numerosos jóvenes y estudiantes . También se han instalado varias carpas y algunas lonas para protegerse de la lluvia. Según el Ayuntamiento, unas 450 personas participan en la protesta en plaza Catalunya.

Simón, Daniel y Raül , los tres de Barcelona, son estudiantes y han querido sumarse a la acampada porque consideran que es una problemática "que afecta a todo el mundo". Según explican, la "lucha" lleva tiempo desarrollándose, pero ahora "ha cogido impulso". Uno de ellos ha admitido que, como estudiantes que viven en casa de sus padres en la capital catalana, el problema todavía no les afecta directamente, "pero en un futuro cercano, sí".

Lucia Palomo , de Lleida, ha explicado que es estudiante universitaria y que vive en una residencia en Barcelona. Considera que la acampada se ha inspirado en la que se lleva a cabo en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid , y la ha definido como un canto a la "esperanza".

Por último, Maria y Paula , la primera de Barcelona y la segunda de Palma, han destacado que han recibido el apoyo de sus familias para sumarse a la protesta, con frases como "me parece muy bien que los jóvenes hagáis esto", en palabras de Maria.

"Motivos sobran. Yo vivo en Cerdanyola porque ya no puedo vivir en Barcelona" , ha explicado Paula, que considera que no se trata únicamente de un problema de la capital catalana, "sino que todas las grandes ciudades están igual".
sources.headline: La acampada por la vivienda en Barcelona se cuadruplica y llega a 200 tiendas

sources.body:
Esta mañana, hacia las 11 horas , más de 60 personas se han concentrado ante la sede de Junts per Catalunya , en la calle Marina de Barcelona, para protestar por el rechazo del partido al decreto de vivienda impulsado por el Gobierno. La movilización, convocada por colectivos de vivienda, ha obligado a cortar el tráfico en el tramo de la calle Marina entre Aragó y València, mientras los asistentes hacían sonar silbatos y coreaban consignas para reclamar una vivienda digna.

Parte de los manifestantes han llegado desde la acampada instalada desde el martes en plaza Catalunya , que mantiene su calendario de movilizaciones para reclamar medidas ante la emergencia habitacional. En la protesta también han participado miembros del Sindicat de Llogateres, que han repartido octavillas para la manifestación convocada este sábado en L'Hospitalet, así como integrantes de la PAHC.

Los Mossos d'Esquadra han desplegado un dispositivo ante la sede del partido y han bloqueado el acceso al passatge Bofill, donde se encuentra el edificio de Junts.

Concentración frente a la sede de Junts en Barcelona ante el posible voto en contra del decreto de vivienda, cuya votación está prevista en las próximas horas. / MANU MITRU / EPC

Durante la protesta han seguido a través de unos altavoces instalados en la calle Marina la intervención de la portavoz de Junts en el Congreso, Míriam Nogueras , en la que ha explicado los motivos por los que la formación ha rechazado los decretos relacionados con vivienda.

Durante el discurso, los manifestantes han respondido con silbidos y gritos de “¡Vergüenza, vergüenza!” . Al finalizar la intervención, cuando Nogueras ha confirmado que Junts no votaría a favor de la iniciativa, la protesta ha aumentado con una nueva pitada y más consignas contra el partido.

Durante el acto, representantes de los colectivos de vivienda han cargado contra la gestión de los partidos políticos ante la crisis habitacional. Desde la CNT, uno de los portavoces ha denunciado que “miles de personas han muerto por esta emergencia habitacional” y ha reclamado a las formaciones políticas que den respuesta a las demandas sociales.

“Hay un descontento brutal. Con un salario digno no podemos tener un lugar donde vivir en nuestras condiciones”, ha señalado durante su intervención, en la que también ha llamado a mantener la movilización en la acampada de plaza Catalunya.

Por su parte, un representante de la PAHC ha criticado el rechazo de Junts al decreto y ha reivindicado que “nosotros también somos Catalunya y tenemos problemas”. El portavoz ha pedido mantener la unidad entre los colectivos de vivienda y ha reclamado que la problemática de los desahucios tenga más visibilidad.

Un representante de la CNT atiende a los medios de comunicación durante la protesta ante la sede de Junts. / MANU MITRU / EPC

Pasadas las 12.30 horas, los organizadores han llamado a los asistentes a movilizarse hacia el barrio del Raval para intentar parar un desahucio previsto para este viernes. Los manifestantes han pedido reforzar la protesta y mantener la presión en la calle ante lo que consideran una emergencia habitacional.
sources.headline: Decenas de manifestantes presionan a Junts en su sede de Barcelona por la votación del ‘decreto Maricarmen’

stories.headline: Flooding in the Terres de l’Ebre disrupts rail service and leads to school suspensions

sources.body:
Actuación de los Bombers de la Generalitat en el puerto de l'Ametlla de Mar, esta tarde de jueves, alertados por el temporal. / Bombers

Las tormentas han empezado a descargar con fuerza este jueves en el sur de Catalunya . Las lluvias han dejado registros de hasta 80 litros por metro cuadrado en la isla de Buda (Montsià) y de 68 en la Bisbal del Penedès (Baix Penedès) en una jornada en la que, ya por la noche, Protecció Civil ha vuelto a enviar una nueva Es-Alert a los municipios de Montsià, Baix Ebre, Ribera d'Ebre y Baix Camp ante el riesgo por un temporal que puede dejar hasta 200 litros por metro cuadrado. La situación de peligro se alargará desde esta medianoche hasta mañana viernes al mediodía . El aviso ha obligado a cancelar las clases en numerosos municipios del Ebro.

Durante toda la jornada, Protecció Civil ha pedido extremar las precauciones y la autoprotección, especialmente en el Ebro, donde las previsiones apuntan a que el temporal podría ir acompañado de piedras de granizo de más de dos centímetros, fuertes rachas de viento y tornados . Ante la alerta, se han suspendido servicios ferroviarios de larga distancia entre Barcelona y València , una afectación que también se ha extendido a otros trenes en Tarragona . El episodio afecta al sur de Catalunya y a la costa valenciana, especialmente a la provincia de Castelló.

A última hora de la tarde, el Meteocat ha actualizado el aviso por intensidad de lluvia y ha situado el mayor riesgo a partir de medianoche y hasta las 14:00 h del viernes. La zona más afectada por la alerta roja (peligro de 5 sobre 6) son las Terres de l'Ebre y el Baix Camp, donde la intensidad de lluvia puede superar los 40 litros en media hora. De hecho, al cierre de esta edición, varias ciudades y pueblos de las Terres de l’Ebre ya han acumulado grandes cantidades de agua , debido a la persistencia de las precipitaciones , que poco antes de la medianoche se han quedado concentradas sobre el Montsià y el Baix Ebre.

De hecho, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) también ha emitido varios avisos rojos por chubascos muy fuertes y persistentes que podrían llegar a acumular 90 mm en una hora y de 250 mm en 12 horas hasta el mediodía de este viernes.

Protecció Civil teme especialmente la posibilidad de que las lluvias intensas queden estacionadas durante la madrugada de este viernes en puntos de las Terres de l'Ebre en un episodio que podría dejar 200 litros por metro cuadrado y que ha obligado a enviar una alerta a los móviles en las comarcas de la Terra Alta, el Baix Ebre y el Montsià. "Se puede superar el umbral de 90 mm en tres horas, lo que nos da la idea de un aguacero de grandes cantidades", ha apuntado Santi Segalà , jefe de predicción del Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya.

Ante esta situación, ayuntamientos ebrenses como Deltebre, Alcanar, La Ràpita, Masdenverge, Tortosa, Santa Bàrbara y Freginals han optado por cancelar las clases este jueves y algunos también el viernes. Algunos consistorios –es el caso de Tortosa y L'Ametlla de Mar – han cerrado los equipamientos municipales. Protecció Civil también ha informado, pasadas las 23:00 horas, de que 4.300 usuarios del Baix Ebre se habían quedado sin suministro eléctrico a causa de las lluvias.
sources.headline: El temporal deja inundaciones y cortes ferroviarios en Tarragona y obliga a suspender clases en el Ebro

sources.body:
Atascos en la entrada de Barcelona desde la B-20 de Santa Coloma. / Zowy Voeten / EPC

EL PERIÓDICO ofrece en este directo la última hora del tráfico y la movilidad en Catalunya , con especial atención al episodio de lluvias e inundaciones que está afectando al sur de Tarragona. Sigue en tiempo real las retenciones, accidentes, carreteras cortadas e incidencias que afectan a las principales vías de circulación.

El directo recoge también las afectaciones en Rodalies y otros servicios de transporte público , además de las recomendaciones y avisos de Protección Civil que puedan condicionar los desplazamientos durante la jornada.

Por petición de los Bombers, no circulan trenes entre Tarragona y Ulldecona debido a las inundaciones en la zona, informa Rodalies.

La circulación es mayoritariamente fluida en las carreteras de la provincia de Barcelona, con algunas retenciones puntuales.

Hay tráfico lento en la B-10 , tanto en sentido norte, en el nudo de la Trinitat, como en sentido sur, en el entorno del nudo del Llobregat, y también en la B-20 hacia el sur.

En la A-2 , a la altura de Esparreguera, las obras obligan a cortar un carril y provocan retenciones.

También hay circulación intensa en la AP-7 en Barberà del Vallès, en sentido sur, y en la BV-1415 , en Collserola en el término de Cerdanyola del Vallès, donde unos desprendimientos obligan a establecer paso alternativo. Estos los provocaron las lluvias del martes.

Las inundaciones mantienen varios tramos de carretera cerrados en el sur de Tarragona, especialmente en el Baix Ebre y el Montsià. Entre las principales afectaciones está la N-340, cortada entre Alcanar y Amposta en un tramo de 20 kilómetros .

También siguen cerradas la TV-3421 entre Mas de Barberans y Roquetes (15 km) , la TP-3311 entre la Galera y la Sénia (14 km) , la T-331 entre Freginals y Tortosa (11 km) y la C-42 entre Tortosa y l’Aldea (10 km) .

Además, permanecen cortadas la T-1025 entre Mas de Barberans y Santa Bàrbara (6 km) , la TP-3318 entre Alcanar y Ulldecona (5 km) y dos tramos de la C-12 , entre Tortosa y Roquetes (4 km) y en Amposta (1 km).

Protección Civil alerta de posibles crecidas súbitas de ríos y rieras en la Ribera d’Ebre y el Baix Ebre , a partir de los avisos hidrológicos de la Agència Catalana de l’Aigua.

Pide extremar la precaución en l’Ametlla de Mar, Tivissa, el Perelló y l’Ampolla , y evitar cauces, vados, accesos a los ríos y zonas bajas.

Protección Civil ha activado la fase de emergencia del plan INUNCAT por las precipitaciones registradas, la previsión de que continúe lloviendo durante las próximas horas y las incidencias que ya se están produciendo en el Baix Ebre y el Montsià .

Protección Civil pide evitar los desplazamientos y seguir las indicaciones de las autoridades en todo momento.

Proteccin Civil activa la prealerta FERROCAT ante posibles inundaciones en la vía de la línea R16 . La circulación ferroviaria está cortada ahora entre Tarragona y Ulldecona por el episodio de lluvias.

Protecció Civil alerta de la crecida del barranc de la Galera , un curso de agua que atraviesa varios municipios del Montsià. El barranco recoge agua de Mas de Barberans, pasa por la Galera y se acerca a Masdenverge antes de llegar al Ebro.
sources.headline: Directo | Las inundaciones complican la movilidad en Tarragona con carreteras cortadas y afectaciones en Rodalies
